title: The Social Divide of Social Distancing: Shelter-in-Place Behavior in Santiago During the Covid-19 Pandemic
eligible_reason: Main-text staggered-lockdown specification (Table 2) interacts the lockdown treatment with socioeconomic-group shares (subgroup-by-treatment interactions) and uses a fractional-days, on-and-off treatment. Table 3 uses continuous mobility as the regressor. No qualifying main-text specification.
design_notes: Table 2 / Eq. (3): log(Mobility_it) = delta_i + sum_s tau_ts*D_is + sum_s beta_s*D_is*LockLocal_it + u_it. Zone FE, week-by-SEG-share coefficients (week FE interacted with time-invariant SEG shares), robust SEs. LockLocal_it = fraction of days in week t that zone i is under a localized lockdown, set to 0 during the citywide lockdown (from week 20), so the treatment switches on (group 1: March 27-30, group 2: late April) and off (group 1 lifted mid-April, all set to zero after May 15). Three treatment coefficients, one per SEG (Table 2: -0.089/-0.084/-0.060 for log MobOut; -0.303/-0.112/-0.155 for log MobRisk; N=29,214). Table 3 (municipality and week FE, 411 obs) regresses log R_kt on lagged mobility (continuous) with LockLocal only as a control in cols (5)-(6). A parsimonious homogeneous-effect version of Eq. (3) is mentioned as being in Appendix F, which is not in the extracted text and is not main text.
estimators_reported: TWFE with group-specific treatment effects and week x SEG-share effects

ineligible_specs.location: Table 2 col (1) (log MobOut) and col (2) (log MobRisk), three coefficients each
ineligible_specs.reason: subgroup-by-treatment interactions (LockLocal x HighSEG/MedSEG/LowSEG); fractional-days treatment that switches off
ineligible_specs.note: Appendix F homogeneous-effect version could be reconsidered only if the protocol counts appendix specs, which it does not

ineligible_specs.reason: continuous mobility treatment (lagged); LockLocal used as control; outcome log growth rate; threshold sample

screener_notes: Infections, lockdown dates and census data are public (Chilean Ministry of Health and Science, 2017 Census). Mobility data come from a private mobile-phone provider and are proprietary. Text excludes the appendix and data-availability section. Flag from 'staggered' in Section 3.1 describing identification.
